mechanism.level_data_directory: ARITHMETIC, no table: dir = scene_id <= 10 ? scene_id : scene_id - 10 (slti @0x8003D204, addiu -10 @0x8003D214); ori 0x0140 @0x8003D218 selects the LEVEL1.* variant for scene_id >= 11.
mechanism.sound_bank: FUNC_8003CF2C computes jumptable[scene_id-1] (bounds sltiu <17 @0x8003CF88, table 0x8001AFB0) and jumps to a per-scene handler; the 0x8001AD0C string it reaches is a VAB/SOUND-BANK prefix, NOT a level-data path.
mechanism.provenance: This law was banked by Phase 3 on 2026-08-01 (analysis/phase3_scene_asset_graph.json, 'law'). Re-pinned here from the image. The first version of this artifact wrongly presented 0x8001AD0C as the level-data path.
mechanism.note: The two tables are PERMUTED. Indexing 0x8001AD0C at scene_id-1 quotes another scene's sound bank.

f08_corrected_binding.was_claimed: scene_asset_table[4] = level10\level2b -- [4] is a JUMP-TABLE index and that string is scene id 10's sound bank

residency_method: offline: RAM extracted from the .sav container (zstd), overlay identified by >=2 agreeing high-entropy code slices; zero-vs-zero byte agreement excluded (LEVEL05 99.14%% over 1862 non-trivial bytes vs LEVEL10 5.53%%). LEVEL10_LEVEL.BIN is NOT resident anywhere in a scene-5 save.
false_positive_note: LEVEL09_LEVEL1.BIN also slice-matches in several saves but at a WANDERING base (0x800B3990/39BC/39CC); the true overlay is always exactly 0x800B39A0. Base stability is the discriminator.
why_it_went_unnoticed: Only scene ids 1 and 15 satisfy index == id-1. F15_canyon_showdown uses id 15, so its binding is correct BY COINCIDENCE and was additionally corroborated live by D20's transferLog resolution to LEVEL05/LEVEL1.DAT. That correct-looking row is not evidence for the rule.
